latest_nl_proof:
Let X and Y be finite sets, and assume there exists an injective function f : X -> Y. We must prove that |X| <= |Y|.

Because Y is finite, every subset of Y is finite, and its cardinality is at most |Y|. Consider the image f(X) = {f(x) : x in X}. Since f(X) is a subset of Y, it follows that f(X) is finite and
|f(X)| <= |Y|.

Now we use injectivity of f to compare X and f(X). The map f, viewed as a function from X onto f(X), is surjective by definition of image. It is also injective by hypothesis. Hence f : X -> f(X) is a bijection. Therefore X and f(X) have the same cardinality:
|X| = |f(X)|.

Combining the two facts,
|X| = |f(X)| <= |Y|,
so |X| <= |Y|, as required.
role_in_parent: Converts the injection between Kunz layers into the needed inequality of cardinalities.
statement_nl: Let X and Y be finite sets. If there exists an injective function f : X -> Y, then the cardinalities satisfy |X| <= |Y|.
